5 tablespoons sugar or honey: 1.5 litres cold water
A few fresh mint leaves
Wash the lemons well; grate the zest of two without reaching the bitter white pith.
Peel the ginger and slice it thinly.
In a small pan, boil 1 cup of water with the sugar, lemon zest and ginger for 5 minutes; remove from the heat and cool.
Squeeze the juice from all the lemons.
Strain the cooled syrup and mix it in a jug with the lemon juice and the rest of the cold water.
Add the mint leaves and chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
If using honey, add it once the syrup has cooled to lukewarm.
Honey must not be given to babies under 1 year.
Serve cold with ice and a mint leaf.
Keeps 3 days in a closed bottle in the fridge.
Banana oat smoothie
1 teaspoon peanut butter (optional)
Put the oats and milk in the blender jug and leave for 5 minutes to soften.
Peel and slice the banana and add it to the jug.
Add the yoghurt, cinnamon and the optional peanut butter.
Blend for 40–60 seconds until smooth.
If it’s too thick, add a little milk, blend again and serve immediately.
With a frozen banana you get a chilled drink without adding ice.
Leave out the peanut butter if there is a peanut allergy.
Don’t let it stand; it can stay in the fridge for a few hours at most.
Linden tea
2 tablespoons dried linden flowers
1 slice of lemon
1 cinnamon stick (optional)
Boil the water in a teapot.
Add the linden and the optional cinnamon, then turn off the heat.
Leave to steep, covered, for 5–7 minutes; don’t keep boiling it.
Strain into glasses and serve with a lemon slice.
Long boiling makes it bitter; steeping is enough.
Drink herbal teas in moderation in pregnancy and while breastfeeding; ask your doctor before regular use.
Serve hot; add a little honey if you like.
Drink freshly brewed.
Hot apple and cinnamon drink
1 litre water
1 strip of orange peel
Wash the apples, remove the cores and slice thinly.
Put all the ingredients in a pan and bring to the boil.
Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes until the apples are soft.
Take off the heat and let it steep for 5 minutes.
Strain into cups; you can add a few apple slices too.
The apples are usually sweet enough; try it without sugar.
Don’t forget to strain out the cloves.
Serve hot on cold winter days.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat before drinking.
Strawberry kefir
1.5 cups plain kefir
8–10 strawberries
1 teaspoon honey (optional)
Wash the strawberries and remove the stalks.
Put the strawberries and kefir in the blender jug.
Add the honey if you like.
Blend for 30 seconds until smooth and serve immediately.
You can use frozen strawberries.
Honey is not given to children under 1 year.
Serve cold at breakfast or as a snack.
Drink within a few hours of making it.
